To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
serum potentiation of lymphokine cytotoxicity in the patient is related to the level of immunoglobulin in the serum.

(1) neuraminidase immunization is a promising new form of immunotherapy, (2) serum potentiation of lymphocytic cytotoxicity is a useful indicator of response to neuraminidase treatment, and (3) serum blocking of lymphocyte cytolytic activity is a poor indicator of response to immunotherapy.
neuraminidase immunization of patients with melanoma can be associated with a decrease in serum blocking effect and an increase in serum immunoglobuline levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new immunotherapeutic approach, the use of autologous tumor cells altered by the enzyme neuraminidase.
the use of neuraminidase to treat patients with advanced malignancy.
the use of neuraminidase altered autologous tumor cells as immunotherapy for patients with advanced cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neuraminidase immunization is not a panacea, but it is a useful adjunct to the armamentarium of the surgeon treating malignant disease.
the serum blocking effect is associated with a poor prognosis, whereas potentiation is associated with a good prognosis.
neuraminidase immunization of human patients with autologous cells, in a strictly autogenic system, may produce a beneficial response in some patients with cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neuraminidase immunization of patients with advanced cancer may be a successful form of immunotherapy if potentiation of the host response is achieved.
neuraminidase immunization can be successful, and that it can be made even more successful by the use of potentiated serum.
neuraminidase immunization is effective in the treatment of malignant disease in patients with potentiation, but is ineffective or harmful in those with serum blocking.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of serum blocking activity is a bad prognostic sign for patients with melanoma.
the serum factors that influence the outcome of immunotherapy are complex and not yet well understood.
neuraminidase immunotherapeutic protocols should include monitoring of the serum effects on the tumor cell target.
